simple.meaning: כָּחַשׁ (kâchash) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to be untrue , in word (to lie , feign , disown ) or deed (to disappoint , fail , cringe ).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 22 times across Genesis, Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Joshua, 2 Samuel, and 9 more, beginning at Genesis 18:15. Its contexts include covenant, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כָּחַשׁ (H3584).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: כָּחַשׁ (kâchash) / H3584 is traced through Genesis 18:15, Leviticus 5:21, Leviticus 5:22, Leviticus 19:11 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H3584. kachash כָּחַשׁ verb be disappointing, deceive, fail, grow lean (Late Hebrew כָּחַשׁ grow lean ; Hiph`il convict of falsehood, refute ; Aramaic כְּחַשׁ grow lean ; כַּחְשָׁא leanness , כְּחִישׁוּתָא leanness, weakness ; Aph`el as Late Hebrew Hiph`il) — Qal. Perfect 3masculine singular מִשָּׁ֑מֶן כָּחַשׁ וּבְשָׂרִי Psa 109:24 my flesh hath grown lean (away) from fatness (|| מִצּוֺם כָּֽשְׁלוּ בִּרְכַּי ).
